name: Corporate Acquisition Likelihood Model
description: This dataset provides predictive rankings of publicly traded companies most likely to be acquired within the next year. It leverages both advanced natural language processing of global news articles and analysis of structured financial and corporate data, including M&A activity, proxy fights, credit risk, and valuation metrics. By combining text-based signals with fundamental indicators, the model offers percentile scores across global, regional, sector, and industry levels, as well as flags for recent corporate actions. Investors and analysts can use these insights to identify potential takeover targets, anticipate price movements driven by acquisition speculation, and inform event-driven trading strategies.

name: AI Equity Alpha Forecasts
description: This dataset provides machine learning-driven forecasts of total return alpha for a broad universe of listed equities, with prediction horizons ranging from 1 to 12 months. It includes a comprehensive set of 291 explainability factors per stock, spanning areas such as accounting forensics, sentiment analysis, business model clarity, technical indicators, credit risk, valuation models, and more. The dataset delivers both daily and weekly updates, offering granular insights into the drivers of predicted returns. By combining forward-looking alpha scores with detailed factor breakdowns, this resource enables researchers and quantitative analysts to identify potential outperformers, understand the underlying reasons for forecasts, and enhance equity selection and risk management strategies. Its breadth and depth make it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment models.

name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

name: ESG scores
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), facilitating cross-platform security identification and data integration. By linking these two widely used financial identifiers, the dataset enables seamless aggregation and comparison of market data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources. This mapping is essential for portfolio managers, researchers, and trading systems that require accurate and efficient reconciliation of securities across different data vendors. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data integrity and consistency in multi-source financial analysis, which underpins robust quantitative research and trading strategies.

name: Estimations of Key Fundamentals
description: This dataset provides daily, regionally split files containing detailed and consensus analyst estimates for key financial metrics such as revenue, EBITDA, EPS, dividends, and price targets for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes individual analyst and broker forecasts, consensus calculations (mean, median, high, low, standard deviation), and actuals, along with metadata on fiscal periods, reporting currencies, and company identifiers. The dataset is highly granular, supporting point-in-time analysis and backtesting, and is essential for identifying earnings surprises, revisions, and trends in analyst sentiment. By tracking changes in consensus and individual estimates, users can anticipate price movements driven by earnings releases, analyst upgrades/downgrades, and shifts in market expectations.

name: Analyst Trade Ideas
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-platform identification of securities. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring high coverage and accuracy. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, this mapping is essential for data integration, enabling analysts and portfolio managers to link and synchronize datasets from different vendors. By ensuring consistent instrument identification, it supports robust multi-source analytics, backtesting, and the construction of unified trading universes, which are foundational for any quantitative or fundamental price movement analysis.

name: Fundamental Analyst Estimates
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global companies, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. The dataset includes restatements, detailed line items, and standardized fields, enabling robust cross-company and cross-market comparisons. Key fields include balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived ratios such as return on equity, margins, and growth rates. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and predictive modeling, as it allows users to track historical financial performance, identify trends, and build factor models that can help forecast future price movements based on company fundamentals.

name: Analyst Estimates Base Reference
description: This dataset serves as a placeholder or reference point for the foundational data underlying analyst estimates and key performance indicators, without containing any actual financial or market data itself. Its primary function is to facilitate access to industry classifications and essential metadata required for quantitative research, while avoiding penalization for using common base modules in research workflows. Although it does not provide direct content, it enables seamless integration of industry and company classification information, which is crucial for constructing and interpreting analyst-driven signals and for ensuring consistency in backtesting and model development. By supporting the structural backbone for more detailed analyst and KPI datasets, it indirectly aids in the accurate prediction of price movements through proper sector and industry alignment.

name: Global Analyst Earnings Forecasts
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global analyst earnings forecasts, consensus estimates, and actuals for over 60,000 companies, sourced from broker and sell-side analyst submissions. It includes detailed and summary-level data on key financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, and segment-level results, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The dataset tracks both current and historical estimates, revisions, and company-issued guidance, with extensive metadata on contributors, accounting standards, and industry classifications. By aggregating and updating analyst expectations in near real-time, this dataset enables users to monitor market sentiment, identify earnings momentum, and anticipate potential surprises—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Behavioral Finance Signal Factors
description: This dataset provides a suite of behavioral finance-based signals designed to capture investor extrapolation bias in equity markets. It includes six key factors: three that analyze the shape and curvature of price paths, and three that identify salient patterns such as streaks in returns, extreme daily movements, and visually prominent trends. By quantifying how investors may irrationally project recent performance into the future, these signals serve as contrarian indicators and can help forecast short-term reversals and momentum effects. The dataset is valuable for predictive modeling, risk assessment, and portfolio construction, offering insights into market inefficiencies driven by psychological biases and aiding in the identification of potential mispricings and alpha opportunities.

name: China Equity Fundamentals Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental data for companies listed on the China A-share market. It includes key financial metrics such as revenue, net income, assets, liabilities, and other balance sheet and income statement items. By analyzing these fundamental indicators, investors and analysts can assess the financial health, profitability, and growth prospects of listed companies. Such insights are valuable for predicting price movements, identifying undervalued stocks, and making informed investment decisions based on company performance and market trends.

name: China Equity Index Constituents
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on the levels and constituents of a major Chinese equity index, including constituent weights, free float shares, divisors, and corporate actions. By tracking changes in index composition and constituent metrics, analysts can gain insights into market trends, sector rotations, and the impact of corporate actions on index performance. Such data is valuable for building quantitative models, benchmarking portfolios, and predicting price movements based on shifts in index structure and constituent dynamics.

name: China Stock Market Fundamentals
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, multi-dimensional information on Chinese stocks listed on the Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen exchanges. It includes market performance data at various frequencies, detailed corporate actions, and extensive financial statement data such as income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and financial indicators. The dataset covers both historical and point-in-time financials, as well as earning forecasts and notes to financial statements. By integrating market data with corporate and financial fundamentals, it enables in-depth analysis of stock performance, valuation, and corporate events, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements and identifying investment opportunities in the Chinese equity market.

name: China Stock Social Sentiment Scores
description: This dataset provides quantified sentiment scores derived from social media posts and comments related to stocks listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges. Using an AI-driven model, it analyzes the emotional tone—bullish, bearish, or neutral—expressed by investors and key opinion leaders across various platforms. The data includes metrics such as the number of likes, comments, shares, and sentiment probabilities, along with industry and company mentions. By aggregating and tracking sentiment trends, this dataset offers valuable insights into market mood and investor behavior, which can be leveraged to anticipate price movements and inform trading strategies.

name: Price Chart Continuation Pattern Similarity
description: This dataset provides daily, per-stock similarity scores that measure how closely a stock’s price chart matches well-known continuation-style technical patterns, such as flags, pennants, rectangles, channels, scallops, staircases, cup-and-handle, and gap formations. The scores are derived by comparing chart-image embeddings to a curated library of canonical continuation patterns using advanced machine learning techniques. Multiple summary statistics (mean, median, max, dynamic, etc.) are available across different time horizons and regions, enabling flexible analysis. These similarity scores can be used to identify stocks likely to resume their current trend after consolidation, support trend-following strategies, and enhance alpha generation by confirming or filtering trading signals. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative researchers seeking to incorporate pattern-based insights into predictive models for price movement forecasting.

name: Corporate Event Driven Stock Model
description: This dataset provides a systematic stock-selection model that leverages corporate event data and machine learning techniques to predict future stock returns. It incorporates a wide range of event types, such as earnings announcements, executive changes, product launches, and structural corporate actions, and processes them using advanced feature engineering and algorithms like elastic net and xgBoost. The model outputs normalized scores and ranks for stocks based on the predictive impact of these events, enabling users to identify potential alpha opportunities and construct long/short portfolios. By capturing both fundamental and behavioral signals from event-driven market reactions, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, managing risk, and enhancing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

name: Fundamental Point in Time Data
description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 60,000 companies, including both active and inactive firms, with daily granularity. It includes original and restated values for income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as business and geographic segment data, ratios, and company metadata. The point-in-time structure eliminates forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate historical backtesting and model development. With coverage dating back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US, this dataset is essential for constructing robust factor models, event studies, and alpha signals based on true historical financials, supporting reliable prediction of price movements and risk assessment.

name: A-shares Fundamental Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental data for companies listed as A-shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges in China. It includes detailed financial statements such as balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements, along with key financial indicators, valuation metrics (like PE, PB, PS ratios), share capital structure, dividend information, and industry classifications. The dataset covers both historical and current data, enabling users to analyze company performance, financial health, and trends over time. Such fundamental data is essential for building quantitative models, conducting equity research, and predicting price movements, as it allows investors to assess intrinsic value, identify undervalued or overvalued stocks, and monitor changes in company fundamentals that may signal future price action.

name: Hong Kong Fundamental Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental financial data for all China-based companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, spanning all industry sectors. It includes detailed company financial statements, key metrics, shareholder information, market data, and segment analysis mapping. The data is systematically collected and standardized, offering point-in-time and ongoing updates. By enabling deep analysis of revenue, expenses, profitability, and ownership structure, this dataset is highly valuable for investors and analysts seeking to assess company health, identify value opportunities, and predict price movements based on changes in financial performance and market positioning.

name: China Fundamentals
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental financial data for all China-based companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, spanning all industry sectors. It includes detailed company financial statements, key metrics, and market data such as income, expenses, assets, liabilities, and daily closing prices. The data is systematically collected and standardized, offering both historical and point-in-time (PIT) coverage. This rich set of financial indicators enables in-depth analysis of company performance, sector trends, and valuation metrics, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements, constructing factor models, and supporting both quantitative and fundamental investment strategies in the Hong Kong equity market.

name: Company Fundamental Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time global company fundamental data, capturing daily snapshots of financial statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and key ratios as they were known to the market at each historical date. It includes restatements, amendments, and all changes, ensuring accurate backtesting and minimizing look-ahead bias. The dataset covers a wide range of standardized and normalized financial metrics across regions and industries, making it a critical resource for quantitative research, factor modeling, and alpha generation. By reflecting the true information set available to investors at any given time, it enables robust prediction of price movements and supports the development of systematic investment strategies.

name: Global Insider Transaction Features
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, structured features derived from global insider transactions, including purchases, sales, awards, and option exercises by company executives, directors, and major shareholders. It covers multiple regions and asset classes, with detailed metadata such as transaction type, insider role, ownership connection, trade significance, and post-transaction holdings. By aggregating and analyzing these transactions, the dataset enables the identification of potentially informative trades, such as opportunistic buying or selling, which can signal future price movements due to information asymmetry. Quantitative models and event studies built on this data can help forecast abnormal returns, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted portfolio performance by leveraging the predictive power of insider activity.

name: CSI1000 and Risk Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on the CSI 500 Index, which tracks 500 mid-cap A-share companies listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges in China. It includes index levels, constituent lists, constituent weights, free float shares, market capitalization, sector and industry breakdowns, and details on corporate actions such as dividends, rights issues, and share changes. The dataset is valuable for analyzing the performance and structure of the Chinese mid-cap equity market, constructing custom portfolios, and monitoring sector rotation and market trends. By offering granular data on index composition and historical changes, it enables users to assess market breadth, liquidity, and the impact of corporate events, which are critical for predicting price movements and developing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Financial Market News Sentiment
description: This dataset aggregates and processes news articles from over 200 finance, economics, industry, and government sources, including social media and official company accounts. It provides detailed metadata for each news item, such as publication time, source, and relevance to specific companies, along with sentiment analysis and relevance scoring. The data is deduplicated, classified, and tagged with industry and event types, enabling users to track news flow, sentiment trends, and rumor responses at the company and sector level. By quantifying news sentiment and relevance, the dataset offers valuable signals for predicting short-term price movements and market reactions, supporting both quantitative and qualitative investment strategies.

name: Multi Factor Model Universal Output
description: This dataset provides the output of proprietary multi-factor risk models in a standardized format compatible with widely used risk models such as Barra and Uber. It enables portfolio managers and researchers to access daily, point-in-time factor exposures, risk estimates, and groupings for US equities, facilitating integration with simulation and portfolio construction tools. The dataset leverages advanced machine learning clustering techniques on company fundamentals and price data to create robust, dynamically updated groupings that capture stock co-movement and risk structure beyond static sector classifications. By offering comprehensive, daily-updated risk model outputs, this dataset supports more accurate risk control, portfolio optimization, and alpha signal neutralization, ultimately helping users better predict and manage price movements and portfolio risk.

name: Alternative technical factor models
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across major financial data platforms. By facilitating accurate instrument identification, it supports data normalization and aggregation from multiple sources, which is essential for building robust multi-source trading models, conducting security-level research, and ensuring consistency in price and volume analytics. While not directly predictive, this mapping is a foundational resource for linking datasets that can be used to forecast price movements and enhance quantitative research workflows.

name: Stock Selection from Accounting-based Factors
description: This dataset contains a comprehensive suite of Performance Deviation Index (PDI) factors derived from 14 key accounting variables, designed to measure the deviation of a company's latest financial metrics from its historical averages. The dataset includes composite models, quality-focused variants, and sector-neutralized signals, all constructed using advanced techniques such as risk parity weighting, deseasonalization, and clustering. By capturing anomalies and behavioral biases in financial statement data, these factors have demonstrated superior risk-adjusted returns compared to traditional accounting ratios and growth metrics. The dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to enhance stock selection, improve portfolio diversification, and boost predictive power for price movements across global equity markets.

name: Quant Model Data
description: This dataset aggregates a wide range of quantitative metrics and valuation models, focusing on consensus estimates, analyst ratings, institutional forecasts, and historical price data. It includes detailed fields for changes in consensus estimates over various timeframes, analyst sentiment indices, earnings forecasts, valuation ratios, and composite scores that rank securities against their peers. The data is structured to provide insights into market expectations, analyst sentiment, and valuation momentum, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements by identifying securities with strong upward or downward consensus trends, rating changes, and valuation gaps. The comprehensive nature of the dataset allows for robust cross-sectional analysis and can be used to enhance predictive models for stock selection and timing.

name: Stock Selection DL model
description: This dataset provides the outputs of a next-generation deep learning model designed for global stock selection with a focus on statistical arbitrage and mean reversion alpha. It includes both raw and processed model scores, updated daily and with monthly historical data, covering a broad universe of equities across multiple regions. The model leverages advanced neural network architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, transformers, and conformers, and is engineered to be interpretable and relatively uncorrelated with common equity style factors. The dataset is particularly valuable for systematic and high-frequency trading strategies, as it offers timely, actionable signals that can be used to enhance portfolio construction, manage risk, and exploit short-term price inefficiencies. By providing robust, data-driven alpha signals, this dataset can help predict price movements and improve trading performance.

name: Asia Technical and Fundamental ranking model
description: This dataset provides comprehensive daily fundamental analysis and equity ratings for over 40,000 companies across Asian markets. It includes a wide range of metrics such as implied valuation, price ranges, relative valuation to peers, share price performance classifications, and detailed breakdowns of operating models, earnings leverage, margin drivers, and growth expectations. The dataset also covers corporate actions like dividend changes, share buybacks, and M&A activity, as well as assessments of accounting quality, dividend quality, and sustainability of returns. By offering both quantitative scores and qualitative classifications, this dataset enables investors and analysts to identify undervalued or overvalued stocks, spot companies with strong or deteriorating fundamentals, and anticipate potential price movements based on changes in financial health, corporate actions, and peer-relative performance.

name: Macro Economic Event Data
description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events, focusing on developments that are likely to move markets. The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as timing, company identifiers, and industry classification. By offering structured, noise-filtered news with intelligent tagging, this dataset enables quantitative models and event-driven strategies to quickly identify and react to market-moving information, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term price movements and volatility.

Each event is categorized by importance and topic, allowing for integration into quantitative models and historical trend analysis. By tracking and analyzing these significant corporate events, researchers and investors can better anticipate price movements, identify event-driven trading opportunities, and enhance alpha generation strategies.

name: News Analytic Model Data

name: Retail trading activities from Virtual Portfolios
description: This dataset aggregates daily rebalancing actions from over 1.6 million Chinese retail investors using virtual portfolios since 2013, covering more than 100 million buy and sell transactions. It provides detailed metrics such as the number of users and portfolios buying or selling each stock, portfolio weights, traded shares, transaction prices, and user experience levels. By tracking sentiment-like indicators (e.g., net buy/sell users, first-time buyers) and confidence metrics, the dataset offers a unique lens into retail investor behavior and conviction. These insights can be used to gauge market sentiment, identify momentum shifts, and anticipate price movements in A-share stocks, making it a valuable resource for quantitative models and trading strategies focused on retail-driven market dynamics in China.

name: Chinese Equity Relation Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping of the supply chain relationships for China A-share listed companies, leveraging a proprietary industry and product classification system that covers over 4,000 product types and 12 hierarchical layers. It details upstream and downstream connections between products and companies, and includes product-level income and gross profit data for more than 3,700 companies. By revealing the structure and financial significance of supply chain links, the dataset enables investors to identify key suppliers, customers, and industry dependencies. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as disruptions or growth in one part of the supply chain can have ripple effects across related companies and sectors, making it a powerful tool for risk assessment, thematic investing, and alpha generation in the Chinese equity market.

name: Snapshot Grouping Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive reference information for all A-share listed companies in mainland China, including security master details, industry classifications from multiple sources (Wind, CITICS, SEC), historical and current company names, and cross-listed securities mapping (e.g., Hong Kong tickers). It covers essential fields such as company identifiers, listing details, business scope, ownership type, and sector codes, enabling robust universe definition, clustering, and sector-based analysis. By integrating industry classification and related securities data, the dataset supports factor modeling, peer group analysis, and cross-market research, making it valuable for predicting price movements through sector rotation, event studies, and fundamental screening.

name: Chart Pattern Similarity Scores
description: This dataset provides daily similarity scores that quantify how closely a stock’s recent price chart matches a range of canonical bilateral technical patterns, such as triangles, wedges, V-formations, and gap structures. By leveraging advanced image-based embeddings of OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data, the dataset compares current price action to a curated library of reference patterns, producing scores for each pattern and aggregation method (mean, max, quantile, etc.) across multiple time horizons and global regions. These similarity scores help researchers and traders identify when a stock is exhibiting chart formations that historically precede significant price moves, either as continuations or reversals. The dataset is particularly valuable for developing and validating quantitative trading signals (alphas), as it enables systematic pattern recognition, supports cross-sectional and multi-horizon analysis, and can be integrated into machine learning models to enhance predictive power for future price movements.

name: Deep Learning Price Signal Dataset
description: This dataset provides stock-level trading signals generated by optimizing traditional price and volume indicators using deep learning techniques. By rescaling and refining these indicators based on the unique properties of each instrument, the dataset aims to deliver uncorrelated alpha signals that enhance returns and Sharpe ratios. The data includes processed price, volume, and derived metrics, with robust handling of outliers and missing values. This resource is valuable for quantitative analysts and traders seeking to improve predictive accuracy and risk-adjusted performance in equity markets.

name: Microstructure Spread Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive spread pricing data for securities traded across the US, Canada, and Asia. It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

name: Corporate Bond Pricing Data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of equity signals derived from corporate bond pricing data, including z-spread curves, term spreads, and principal component analysis factors such as shift, tilt, and twist. By linking bond market indicators—such as credit risk, yield curve dynamics, and bond-equity return divergences—to related equities, the dataset offers 19 base factors and several variants to predict future stock returns. These factors capture changes in credit conditions, market sentiment, and cross-asset relationships, making the dataset valuable for quantitative models, risk assessment, and alpha generation. Investors and analysts can use these signals to enhance equity selection, construct long-short strategies, and anticipate price movements based on underlying credit market trends.

name: A-shares Index Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental and market data for China A-shares indices, including basic index descriptions, end-of-day prices, industry classifications, index constituents, ETF creation and redemption details, and member weights for exchange indices. It covers a wide range of financial metrics such as market capitalization, valuation ratios (PE, PB, PS), trading volumes, turnover rates, and corporate actions. The dataset also includes information on index rebalancing, constituent changes, and sector mappings, making it a valuable resource for analyzing market structure, sector rotation, and price drivers. By integrating index-level fundamentals with constituent and industry data, this dataset enables robust factor modeling, backtesting, and prediction of price movements in the Chinese equity market.

name: A-shares Trade Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive daily trading data for China A-shares, including price, volume, turnover, money flow, margin trading, block trades, insider trades, shareholder changes, and technical indicators. It covers end-of-day prices, abnormal trades, order book statistics, and detailed breakdowns by trader type and transaction size. The data enables analysis of liquidity, market impact, order flow, and trading patterns, supporting quantitative models for price prediction, momentum, mean reversion, and risk management. By capturing both standard and unusual trading activity, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, identifying volume-driven return premiums, and understanding market microstructure effects in the Chinese equity market.

name: Derived Industry Classification
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, two of the most widely used security identifiers in the financial industry. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from different sources, facilitating more accurate and efficient data analysis. This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is essential for data normalization, aggregation, and the construction of robust multi-source trading and risk models.

name: Alternate Industry Classification
description: This dataset provides an alternative industry classification for global equities, derived from historical stock returns using principal component analysis (PCA) and robust resampling methods. By extracting significant risk factors and grouping securities into clusters of varying sizes, it offers a data-driven approach to industry segmentation across multiple regions and sectors. The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

name: Specific return of extended factors
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of analyst earnings estimates, company-issued guidance, and actual reported financials for over 60,000 companies. It includes both detailed and consensus forecasts for key financial metrics such as EPS, revenue, cash flow, and dividends, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The data is updated daily and includes historical records, point-in-time snapshots, and restated values to avoid look-ahead and survivorship bias. Industry classification is available via TRBC, and the dataset supports granular analysis by region, sector, and fiscal period. By tracking estimate revisions, consensus trends, and the relationship between guidance and market expectations, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements around earnings announcements, identifying sentiment shifts, and constructing alpha models based on analyst behavior and forecast dispersion.

name: China Stock Search Sentiment Index
description: This dataset provides daily search volume analytics for CSI500 and CSI300 stocks, using search engine data as a proxy for investor interest in the Chinese equity market. By tracking the frequency and intensity of stock-related keyword searches, the dataset captures shifts in public attention and sentiment toward individual companies and sectors. Such search-based sentiment indicators can serve as leading signals for price movements, as spikes in search activity often precede changes in trading volume, volatility, and market direction. The dataset is particularly valuable for short-term forecasting, event-driven strategies, and understanding behavioral trends among retail and institutional investors in China.

name: Website Popularity Rankings
description: This dataset provides a robust, research-oriented ranking of the most popular websites worldwide, designed to be resistant to manipulation and volatility. It aggregates and harmonizes data from multiple sources, including DNS traffic, browser extensions, and web crawls, to produce a stable and reproducible list of top domains. The dataset includes detailed metrics such as relative popularity, ranking intervals, domain counts, and statistical measures like skewness and kurtosis. By mapping domains to standardized identifiers, it enables aggregation and analysis at various levels. This dataset is valuable for predicting price movements by identifying trends in web traffic, shifts in user behavior, and the emergence of influential domains, which can signal changes in market sentiment, consumer interest, or sector performance.

name: Daily Price Limit Data
description: This dataset provides daily information on stock trading halts and price limits for equities listed on the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong exchanges, including constituents of the CSI 300 index. It contains fields such as security identifiers, exchange codes, trade dates, and the maximum and minimum allowable prices for each stock on a given day. By tracking when stocks hit their limit up or limit down prices, as well as when trading is halted, the dataset helps identify periods of abnormal market activity, liquidity constraints, and potential price reversals. Such insights are valuable for predicting short-term price movements, managing trading risk, and developing quantitative strategies sensitive to market imbalances.

name: Sentiment Data for Equity
description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes social media posts and news articles related to financial markets, covering thousands of sources and several years of historical data. It quantifies market sentiment and buzz for individual assets, sectors, and indices using advanced natural language processing and machine learning techniques. The data includes sentiment scores, buzz indicators, and trading signals, which are statistically validated and can be used to identify shifts in market mood, anticipate volatility, and generate actionable buy/sell signals. By monitoring real-time and historical sentiment, traders and analysts can enhance their price movement predictions and improve portfolio performance through timely, data-driven decisions.
